newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian town calm after post-election rampage.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian town calm after post-election rampage.

text.p: Thousands of Indonesians on the Madura island off Java's east coast burned a housing complex, offices and a church on Thursday night as general elections results showed the ruling Golkar party taking a huge lead, police and residents said on Friday. Police said government offices, a teachers' housing complex and other houses were among buildings burned or attacked

JAKARTA, May 30 (Reuter) - Thousands of Indonesians on the Madura island off Java's east coast burned a housing complex, offices and a church on Thursday night as general elections results showed the ruling Golkar party taking a huge lead, police and residents said on Friday. Police said government offices, a teachers' housing complex and other houses were among buildings burned or attacked by the rioters, but the situation had returned to normal since in the Madurese town of Sampang.
"They also attacked shops and burned some of them," a police official told Reuters. "Less than 100 buildings and houses were either burned or attacked." He declined to give further details.
Residents said the riots were sparked by the general election results, which put Golkar way ahead of the other two parties allowed to take part in the polls.
Madura is strongly Moslem and a stronghold of the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP). Most of the pre-election violence in Indonesia was between partisans of Golkar and the PPP.
President Suharto's Golkar was headed for a landslide win with more than half the potential ballots counted on Friday.
By Friday morning with just over half the potential ballots counted, Golkar had 73.87 percent, the PPP 23.30 and the badly-split Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) 2.83 percent of the vote.
